## Zoning Analysis: 3400 N Central Park Ave (PIN 13233160400000)

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3** (Residential Single-Unit, Detached House) per the City's official GIS parcel layer. RS-3 is the most permissive single-family district, distinguished from RS-1 and RS-2 primarily by lower minimum lot area requirements and higher FAR allowances [3].

**Verify:** [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning), search PIN 13233160400000.

---

### 2. Can I Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Possibly, but not by right on every lot.** In RS-3, a two-unit building (two-flat) is generally not a permitted use — the district is intended for detached single-family houses [3]. However, [1] provides a specific exemption: the minimum lot area per unit **may be reduced to 1,500 sq ft** (enabling a two-flat) when **60% or more** of the zoning lots on the same side of the block have been lawfully improved with multi-unit buildings, or when the property falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundaries (§17-7-0591). This exemption only permits a **two-unit building**, not more.

Given that the current building on this parcel has **5 units** (built 1927), the block may already satisfy the 60% threshold — but you would need to confirm actual block conditions through the Department of Buildings or a zoning analysis.

**Verify:** Zoning Administrator, Department of Planning & Development (DPD), or a licensed zoning attorney.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards (RS-3)

The retrieved code text covers density and parking; the full RS-3 bulk table (FAR, height, setbacks) was **not returned** in the retrieved code chunks. Based on [1] and [3]:

- **Minimum lot area per unit:** 2,500 sq ft per unit in RS-3 (standard); reducible to 1,500 sq ft per unit for a two-flat under the conditions in [1].
- **FAR, maximum height, and setback figures** for RS-3 are governed by §17-2-0300 and its associated tables [1], but the specific numeric limits were not in the retrieved text. These must be confirmed directly in the Zoning Ordinance or with DPD.
- **Lot area per unit measurement rules** are governed by §17-17-0304, cross-referenced in [1].

*Note: This parcel has 3,616 sq ft of land area and currently carries 5 units — that is well below the standard 2,500 sq ft/unit RS-3 threshold, suggesting the existing building is a pre-existing nonconforming structure.*

**Verify:** Full RS-3 bulk table at [Chicago Zoning Ordinance §17-2-0400](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago_zoning_ordinance.html) or DPD.

**ARO Housing in Avondale:** Under the Affordable Requirements Ordinance, 6 affordable housing projects totaling 76 units have been developed in the community area, including Hairpin Lofts (25 units, 3414 W. Diversey) and Milwaukee Ave. Apts. (32 units supportive housing, 3060 N. Milwaukee).

**Brownfields nearby:** Two BNSF Little Village Paseo brownfield sites (EPA IDs 110071982538 and 110071982539) are located in the broader area. Environmental due diligence may be advisable for any ground-disturbing work.

**Verify:** DPD overlays and ARO obligations at [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning); ARO details via the Department of Housing.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

This parcel is within a CTA Transit-Oriented Development area (Addison Blue Line station, ~0.25 miles away). Under §17-10-0102-B, the minimum off-street parking requirement **may be reduced by up to 100%** — meaning parking can potentially be waived entirely for this parcel. This relief applies without requiring a special entitlement.

Where parking is provided, RS-3 rules [4] require:
- No parking in side setbacks or within 20 feet of the front property line (except when accessed by a permitted driveway).
- Required residential parking must be on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served [4].

**Important:** The transit-served location does **not** confer any FAR, density, height, or lot-area-per-unit bonus — those bonuses apply only in dash-3 districts (B1-3, B2-3, C1-3, etc.), not RS-3.

**Verify:** §17-10-0102-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance; confirm TOD boundary with DPD.

---

### 6. Coach House / Additional Dwelling Unit (ADU)

**Yes — this parcel is in an ADU Eligible Area**, which means a coach house or conversion ADU may be permitted under [2] (§17-7-0570–0573). Key conditions and limits [5]:

- A new coach house in an RS district requires compliance with §17-7-0570 [5] — pre-certification through the **Department of Housing** is required [2].
- Coach houses **may not exceed 22 feet** in building height [5].
- Rooftop features may not exceed 22 feet above grade [5].
- At least **3 feet of unobstructed open space** must be maintained between the coach house and at least one side property line [5].
- Coach houses may only be in a rear-yard location (in B/C districts, rear 30 feet — RS rules defer to §17-7-0570) [5].
- **No accessory parking is required** to serve the coach house itself [5]; required parking for the principal building may be administratively reduced or waived (§17-13-1003-OO) [5].
- ADU area limitations (conversion unit caps, coach house caps) may apply per §17-7-0573 [2] — confirm the specific limits for this ADU area with the Department of Housing.

**Verify:** Department of Housing ADU pre-certification process; §17-7-0570 [2] and §17-9-0200 [5].

---

### Confidence & Limitations

- **High confidence:** Zoning district (RS-3), overlay designations (TOD, ADU, ARO, Special District), parking reduction eligibility, coach house framework, and property characteristics — all from authoritative city GIS and Cook County Assessor data.
- **Moderate confidence:** Two-flat feasibility — depends on actual block conditions (60% threshold) not verifiable from this data alone.
- **Could not determine:** Specific numeric FAR, maximum height, and setback figures for RS-3 (not returned in retrieved code); specific Special District rules; and the exact ADU area sub-limitations under §17-7-0573 for this location.
